results.question: How did Kimi Antonelli win Monza 2026 from 19th on the grid?
results.answer: Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes, #12) converted a 19th-place grid start into a race victory at Monza 2026 through an aggressive two-stop strategy using Hard and Medium tyres. On lap 3, just two laps into the race, he made an extremely early pit stop (pit duration ~1,842.6s — likely a red-flag/VSC-related stop or a very long stationary period), rejoining on fresh Mediums. He then charged through the field rapidly: by lap 6 he was P8, P6 by lap 7, P4 by lap 12, P3 by lap 13, P2 by lap 16, and P1 by lap 18 — reaching the lead in just 18 laps. He held the lead for the remainder of the 53-lap race, posting a best lap of 1:23.504 and an average of 1:26.605, to take the win having gained 18 positions from his grid slot.

results.question: What were the decisive events of the 2026 Italian Grand Prix race?
results.answer: Kimi Antonelli delivered the race's defining performance, charging from P19 on the grid all the way to victory — an 18-place gain, the most of any driver. Pierre Gasly started from pole (P1) but faded to P7, losing 6 positions across the race. George Russell held P2 from grid to finish, while Max Verstappen climbed from P5 to P3. Charles Leclerc (P3 on grid) and Fernando Alonso (P21) did not record a classified finish, suggesting retirements. Liam Lawson was the second-biggest mover, rising 8 places from P22 to P14.

Norris (McLaren) and Piastri (McLaren) took Hard tyres for a 50-lap stint averaging 1:28.104 and 1:26.640 respectively, while Verstappen (Red Bull) opted for Mediums for 25 laps averaging 1:26.058 — the fastest average of any stint in the data. Russell (Mercedes) also ran a strong 50-lap Hard stint averaging 1:26.378. On the incident front, Perez (Cadillac) and Colapinto (Alpine) were both investigated after the race for practice-start infringements on lap 1, a Turn 2 incident between Leclerc and Hamilton on lap 4 was reviewed but required no further action, and Tsunoda received a deferred investigation for a starting-procedure infringement on lap 11.

results.question: List the safety car, virtual safety car and red flag periods in the 2026 Italian GP race with their laps.
results.answer: The 2026 Italian GP at Monza featured one Safety Car deployment and one Red Flag suspension. The Safety Car was deployed on Lap 3 (at 13:06:49 UTC) following multiple double-yellow flag sectors (14, 15, 16) caused by an incident. Just under a minute later, on Lap 3 (13:07:43 UTC), the race was suspended under a Red Flag. There is no Virtual Safety Car (VSC) period recorded in the data for this race. The race also saw scattered yellow flag sectors on Lap 1 and Lap 3–4 around the circuit.

SELECT
  rc.date,
  rc.lap_number,
  rc.category,
  rc.flag,
  rc.scope,
  rc.sector,
  rc.message,
  rc.driver_number
FROM raw.race_control rc
WHERE rc.session_key = 11361
  AND (
    rc.category ILIKE '%safety%'
    OR rc.flag ILIKE '%safety%'
    OR rc.flag ILIKE '%virtual%'
    OR rc.flag ILIKE '%red%'
    OR rc.message ILIKE '%safety car%'

  )

LIMIT 200

),
stint_info AS (
  SELECT
    ss.driver_number,

results.question: How did Antonelli's gap to Russell change over the last 10 laps of the 2026 Italian GP?
results.answer: Over the final 10 laps (laps 44–53) of the 2026 Italian GP, Antonelli steadily pulled away from his Mercedes teammate Russell. He was consistently faster, building a cumulative gap that grew from -0.784s after lap 44 to -8.588s by the chequered flag on lap 53. The only lap where Russell had the edge was lap 49 (+0.607s to Antonelli), likely due to a blue-flag incident affecting Antonelli. On the final lap alone, Antonelli was nearly 2 seconds quicker (1:23.504 vs 1:25.486), sealing a dominant finish with Antonelli P1 and Russell P2.

WITH total_laps AS (
  SELECT MAX(lap_number) AS max_lap
  FROM core.laps_enriched
  WHERE session_key = 11361
    AND driver_number IN (12, 63)
),
last_10_laps AS (
  SELECT le.lap_number,
         le.driver_number,
         le.driver_name,
         le.lap_duration,
         le.is_pit_lap,
         le.compound_name,
         le.track_flag,
         le.position_end_of_lap
  FROM core.laps_enriched le
  CROSS JOIN total_laps tl
  WHERE le.session_key = 11361
    AND le.driver_number IN (12, 63)
    AND le.lap_number > tl.max_lap - 10
),
pivoted AS (
  SELECT
    a.lap_number,
    a.lap_duration AS antonelli_lap_s,
    r.lap_duration AS russell_lap_s,
    a.is_pit_lap AS antonelli_is_pit_lap,
    r.is_pit_lap AS russell_is_pit_lap,
    a.compound_name AS antonelli_compound,
    r.compound_name AS russell_compound,
    a.track_flag,
    a.position_end_of_lap AS antonelli_position,
    r.position_end_of_lap AS russell_position
  FROM last_10_laps a
  JOIN last_10_laps r ON a.lap_number = r.lap_number
  WHERE a.driver_number = 12
    AND r.driver_number = 63
),
cumulative AS (
  SELECT
    lap_number,
    antonelli_lap_s,
    russell_lap_s,
    ROUND((antonelli_lap_s - russell_lap_s)::numeric, 3) AS lap_time_delta_s,
    ROUND(SUM(antonelli_lap_s - russell_lap_s) OVER (ORDER BY lap_number)::numeric, 3) AS cumulative_gap_s,
    antonelli_is_pit_lap AS is_pit_lap,
    antonelli_compound AS compound_name,
    track_flag,
    antonelli_position,
    russell_position
  FROM pivoted
)
SELECT
  lap_number,
  ROUND(antonelli_lap_s::numeric, 3) AS antonelli_lap_s,
  ROUND(russell_lap_s::numeric, 3) AS russell_lap_s,
  lap_time_delta_s,
  cumulative_gap_s,
  is_pit_lap,
  compound_name,
  track_flag,
  antonelli_position,
  russell_position
FROM cumulative
ORDER BY lap_number
